frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully pass a joint resolution of disapproval to block a 123 agreement?
membership_rule: Includes all formal submitted 123 agreements where Congress had a statutory window to pass a joint resolution of disapproval. Excludes non-nuclear executive agreements and treaties requiring Senate advice and consent.
window: Statutory review windows ranging from 60 to 90 continuous days, evaluated across the post-WWII era through the specified deadline.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 major contested cases named out of approximately 20+ total 123 agreements submitted historically, none of which were successfully blocked by joint resolution.
known_gaps: Minor technical or routine 123 agreements renewing existing terms automatically without congressional friction are excluded from the contested denominator.
skeleton: Total formal 123 agreements submitted for congressional review since the modern statutory framework minus informal withdrawals.
multiplier: 3 historical high-profile contested submissions where a resolution of disapproval was introduced but failed to pass both chambers over presidential veto.
validity_reason: The statutory framework under the Atomic Energy Act remains stable, though political polarization could alter historical deference if majorities align.
